units.source_text: 看到先生花费纸墨写了这么多页的信，我不禁甚为惊异，先生到底写了些什么呢？

en.t: Seeing that Sensei had spent so much paper and ink writing a letter of so many pages, I could not help being deeply astonished, and wondered what on earth he had written.

units.source_text: 同时，我还时时留意着病房的动静。

en.t: At the same time, I kept listening for any movement in the sickroom.

units.source_text: 我预感到，在我没看完这封信之前，父亲一定会出什么事，

en.t: I had a premonition that before I finished reading this letter, something would surely happen to my father,

units.source_text: 至少我会被哥哥或者母亲，不然就是伯父叫去，无法踏踏实实地看完先生的信。

en.t: or at least that my elder brother, my mother, or else my uncle would call me away, making it impossible for me to settle down and read Sensei's letter through.

units.source_text: 我只是心不在焉地看了开头的一页，是这样写的：

en.t: I merely read the first page absentmindedly; it was written as follows:

units.source_text: “当你问起我的过去时，我没有勇气回答你。

en.t: When you asked about my past, I did not have the courage to answer you.

units.source_text: 现在我相信，在你面前，我已经有了清楚地回答你的自由。

en.t: Now I believe that, before you, I have gained the freedom to answer you clearly.

units.source_text: 然而这自由，不过是在等待你回京期间，又将失去的人世间的自由。

en.t: However, this freedom is only a worldly freedom that will be lost again while I wait for you to return to Tokyo.

units.source_text: 因此，如果不在能够利用时加以利用的话，

en.t: Therefore, if I do not make use of it while I am able to use it,

units.source_text: 我就将永远失去把自己的过去作为间接经验告诉你的机会了。

en.t: I will forever lose the chance to tell you about my past as an indirect experience of your own.

units.source_text: 这样一来，我曾经那么坚决地许下的诺言就成了谎言。

en.t: If that happens, the promise I once made so firmly will become a lie.

units.source_text: 不得已，我才把应该亲口告诉你的事，用这封信来告诉你。”

en.t: Having no other choice, I am using this letter to tell you what I ought to have told you in person.

units.source_text: 读到这里，我才明白了先生为什么要给我写这么长的信。

en.t: Only after reading this far did I understand why Sensei had written me such a long letter.

units.source_text: 我一开始就知道，先生是不会为我的糊口问题写这样的信的。

en.t: From the beginning, I knew that Sensei would not write such a letter about my means of making a living.

units.source_text: 然而，一向讨厌动笔的先生，怎么会想起把那件事写得这么长，寄来给我看呢？

en.t: But why had Sensei, who always disliked taking up the pen, decided to write about that matter at such length and send it for me to read?

units.source_text: 为什么不能等我回京再对我说呢？

en.t: Why could he not wait until I returned to Tokyo and tell me then?
Because I am free, I can speak.

units.source_text: 但是这自由又将永远地失去。”

en.t: But this freedom will also be lost forever.
